text: The Problem table extends the base Task table, exactly the same way Incident does. Same base fields, same activity log behavior — what's different is purpose, not plumbing. An Incident is one instance of disruption, a user can't log in right now. A Problem is the underlying cause that may be generating many of those instances at once.

The real link between the two tables is a reference field: problem_id, sitting on the Incident table, pointing at a Problem record. When an agent recognizes a new Incident matches an ongoing investigation, they set problem_id on that Incident — they're pointing at the existing Problem, not duplicating its data into a new record.

That reference field only tells you the relationship from the Incident's side. Open any Problem record, and a related list automatically shows every Incident whose problem_id points back at it — live, with zero manual maintenance required. That's a Problem manager's roster of every affected user, updated continuously. And when the Problem is finally resolved, that same related list is exactly what you use to close the loop: reviewing and updating every linked Incident to reflect that a fix, or at least a workaround, now exists.

The biggest real implementation risk isn't a missing field — it's agents not finding an existing Problem and opening a redundant new investigation instead. Three agents, three separate Problem records for the same VPN disconnect issue, means three sets of investigation notes and no single place where the real fix actually gets documented. A well-implemented instance makes the existing-Problem search fast and obvious: clear naming conventions on short descriptions, an assignment group that triages new Problem candidates, and, once we reach Chapter 5's Knowledge Management coverage, searchable documentation that surfaces a matching Problem before anyone creates a duplicate.

Problem and Incident, connected by one reference field and one related list. Next, we dig into the fields that actually drive the root-cause investigation itself: cause_notes, fix_notes, and the Problem workflow states.
